statement: The package manifest and lockfile declare pg as a production dependency required by the shipped lagrange service lifecycle CLI, while preserving every existing binary, script, dependency version, and package contract.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The only product paths in scope are package.json and package-lock.json. Move the existing exact pg ^8.18.0 declaration from root devDependencies to root dependencies and update npm lock classification for pg and its production dependency closure; do not change versions, resolved artifacts, integrity values, binaries, scripts, exports, engines, or any other dependency declaration.

A production-only npm installation must retain pg and the transitive modules it needs. The root package and lockfile package declarations must agree, pg must be absent from their devDependencies, and the existing lagrange and lagrange-admin executable mappings must remain exact.

The terminal service-init-scaffold scenario remains the behavioral oracle: source and bundled SEA service init plus package binary metadata stay green after dependency reclassification. S5c source imports and lifecycle behavior are explicitly excluded from this companion Quest.

Independent verification must approve the exact two-file patch and aggregate content, prove a production-only dependency-tree check fails when pg is returned to devDependencies or removed from the root lock dependency map, and confirm three consecutive service-init-scaffold scenario runs remain green before checkpoint and handoff.
